cards.text: Jesus has been teaching the crowds about reading the times. Then some people standing there tell Him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate, the governor of Judea (Luke 3:1), had mixed with their sacrifices.

cards.question: Jesus hears about the Galileans Pilate killed at their sacrifices. What does He ask the crowd about them?

answers.text: Were they worse sinners than other Galileans
Did they offer the wrong kind of sacrifices
Why did nobody try to stop Pilate

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd that those Galileans really were worse sinners than all the other Galileans.

cards.text: Jesus says no, they weren't. Then He turns it right back on the crowd, and friend, I know THAT move: you bring up somebody else's burnt batch, and suddenly everybody's looking at YOURS.

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd that unless they ___, they too will all perish.

cards.text: Then Jesus brings up something else. Eighteen people were killed when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them.

cards.question: Jesus asks if the eighteen killed by the tower of Siloam were more sinful than all the others living where?
About the tower of Siloam, Jesus gives the crowd a different warning than the one He gave about the Galileans.

cards.text: Same words, word for word: "No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish." When Jesus says it twice, that's the oven timer going off a SECOND time, and friend, you do NOT wait around for a third.
Then Jesus tells a parable. A man has a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he goes looking for fruit on it.

cards.question: The man goes to his fig tree looking for fruit. What does he find?

cards.text: He tells the keeper of the vineyard he's been coming to search this tree for a while now, and still nothing. I've done that. Open the oven, nothing. Close it. Open it again. STILL nothing.

cards.question: The owner tells the keeper of the vineyard he has searched the fig tree for fruit for the past ___ years.
After all those years with no fruit, what does the owner tell the keeper to do with the fig tree?

cards.text: The owner even asks, 'Why should it use up the soil?' But the keeper of the vineyard has something to say about that.

cards.question: What does the keeper of the vineyard ask the owner to do with the fig tree?

answers.text: Leave it alone one more year
Move it to a sunnier spot
Plant a new tree beside it

cards.question: The keeper of the vineyard plans to leave the fig tree alone and simply wait to see what happens.

cards.text: He'll dig around it and fertilize it, for a tree that hasn't produced one fig in three years. That's me back in the junk drawer, cheering on an expired coupon like it had one more Tuesday left in it.

cards.question: The keeper says if the fig tree bears ___ next year, fine. But if not, the owner can ___ it down.

cards.text: And that's where the parable ends. One more year, and a keeper ready to dig in.
